correctness.rationale: For a Gaussian start, independent chi-square weights of spectral subspaces give the exact polynomial Rayleigh form. The positive spectral moment Gram is positive definite up to q basis vectors by Vandermonde full rank; the single negative eigenvalue contributes a rank-one downdate. Congruence and inertia prove the exact criterion, not just a sufficient bound. Chi-square concentration, matrix inversion continuity, and dominance of the highest monomial establish all critical regimes including zero and infinity; a degree-q positive-band annihilator proves detection at q+1. The strict boundary has zero probability since the isolated Gaussian squared weight is continuous. Direct Krylov tests and the symbolic two-band identity were replayed; the proof, not tests, supports universality.

value.rationale: A natural optimization question is the number of Hessian-vector products needed by an unmodified early-terminated Lanczos probe to reveal a narrow negative-curvature direction. The result supplies a family-wide exact probability, sharp dimension-dependent thresholds for each fixed iteration depth, a striking n to n^(1/3) to n^(1/5) hierarchy, and a finite q+1 deterministic completion. These are motivated accuracy-versus-work tradeoffs, not a one-off arbitrary finite calculation; no guarantee is asserted for modified algorithms.
